solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bother after company curtailed lord in US State

indicators.note: after says the word for bother comes behind the other pieces
curtailed means docked of its tail, so the last letter of lord goes

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
ado is fuss or bother

explanation.surface: A grumble about some aristocrat causing trouble for a firm in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' trims the lord's last letter, and 'after' sets the bother behind the rest; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight description: one of the fifty states of America, in the Rocky Mountains.

clue.text: Note work — quiet work, in police station

parts.note: C is a musical note
op, short for opus, is a musical work
sh is the call for quiet
op again, for opus

explanation.surface: A musician juggling a note and two pieces of work while at a police station.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang term for a local police building, where officers (cops) are based.

clue.text: Commit to memory name of king, northern

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: Memorising the name of a king from the north for a history test.
explanation.definitionFit: To get facts by heart is to acquire them through study.

clue.text: Provide support in motoring competition with drinks for all

parts.note: a rally is a road race for cars
a round is a set of drinks bought for everyone in a group

explanation.surface: Backing a car race by buying everyone drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pubs, buying a round means paying for a drink for each person in the group.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to gather to help someone in need.

clue.text: Part of screed is malicious, dreary

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A reviewer finding a long rant both spiteful and tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy and depressing; dull and cheerless are close synonyms.

clue.text: Good first point

parts.note: 1st, written IST in crosswords, is first

explanation.surface: Someone praising the opening argument of a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: IST stands in for 1ST, the digit 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The essential meaning or main thrust of a matter is its point.

clue.text: Plead with troublemaker, backed by traditional knowledge

indicators.note: backed by says the next piece stands behind the first

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little devil
lore is knowledge handed down by tradition

explanation.surface: Begging a mischief-maker who has folklore on their side.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg or beseech someone earnestly is to make an urgent appeal.

clue.text: Belated thanks, dry, out of order

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

indicators.note: out of order says the letters of dry are not in their proper sequence

explanation.surface: A late thank-you, delivered drily, seen as rude.
explanation.walkthrough: Only DRY is rearranged, to RDY; 'out of order' also hints at rudeness in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Late or slow in arriving, as a delayed reply would be.

clue.text: Music radio station will allow, strangely, past Lily

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of past Lily appear in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A DJ explaining what tracks the station permits, oddly mentioning someone called Lily.
explanation.definitionFit: A station's approved list of songs for broadcast is exactly the music it will allow on air.

clue.text: Encourage sudden effort to knock out finalist?

indicators.note: the finalist here is the final letter of the word, which gets knocked out

parts.note: a spurt is a short burst of effort

explanation.surface: A coach urging a runner's late burst to beat the competitor in the final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finalist' reads as 'final' letter: SPURT loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur someone on is to urge or goad them forward, like a rider's heel.

clue.text: Seize cat if cones knocked over

indicators.note: knocked over suggests the letters are tumbled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A traffic warden threatening to impound a cat that topples road cones.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking property by authority, as customs officers do, is to seize it.

clue.text: Hospital with pharmacy ultimately within easy reach

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital on signs and maps
and can mean with, as in fish and chips

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of pharmacy

explanation.surface: A hospital whose pharmacy is conveniently close by.
explanation.definitionFit: Something handy is conveniently close, available at arm's length.

clue.text: A game, extremely grubby, leads to expression of regret

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback

indicators.note: extremely asks for the two outermost letters of grubby

explanation.surface: A dirty game of sport ends with someone having to say sorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying sorry is a statement conveying remorse for something done.

clue.text: Military detachment's unconvincing role terminated early

definitions.note: read as 'military detachment is', the apostrophe s being the link

parts.note: a pat answer is glib and unconvincing

indicators.note: the word role is ended one letter early, losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A critic panning a soldier's part in a war film as weak and cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: PAT, as in a pat excuse, means too glib to convince. 'terminated early' cuts ROLE to ROL.
explanation.definitionFit: A small squad of soldiers sent out to reconnoitre or guard is such a unit.

clue.text: Doctor on tour including city in Canada

indicators.note: including says the words before it contain the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A travelling doctor whose itinerary takes in a Canadian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' tempts as an anagram signal for 'on tour', but the letters do not fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ontario's capital is the largest Canadian city.

clue.text: Result extremely fortunate for English cricket team, just starting.

indicators.note: just starting asks for only the opening letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A lucky outcome for the England cricket side at the start of a series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like an indicator on 'fortunate' but simply supplies its own first letter, like the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A consequence or outcome of some cause is its result.

clue.text: Tale including rest for a horse?

indicators.note: including says the word rest is taken into the tale
for says it goes in place of the letter a

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A story about stopping for a breather for a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: TALE takes in REST in place of its A. The question mark flags that this horse is not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sawhorse, a frame on legs supporting a board, is a carpenter's horse.

clue.text: Something frosty about for example system of government

indicators.note: about says the frosty word goes around the other piece

parts.note: rime is hoar frost
eg is short for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Describing a cold, unfriendly political order.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruling administration, especially an authoritarian one.

clue.text: Just this time willing to get involved in force

indicators.note: says the word for willing goes into the middle of force

parts.note: to be on for something is to be willing, as in 'I'm on'

explanation.surface: A reluctant recruit agreeing, on this occasion, to join the police force.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means on this single occasion, as an exception to the usual.

clue.text: Bone from female bird, rook

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless bird
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A bone taken from a female crow.
explanation.definitionFit: The thigh bone, the longest in the human body.

clue.text: Examine carefully capacity for action

definitions.meaning: to look something over, as in 'size up' or check out
the range or opportunity available for doing something

explanation.definitionFit: To size something up is to look it over; separately, room to operate is one's range.

clue.text: Tree, more promising, topped

indicators.note: topped means having its top cut off, so the first letter goes in a down entry

parts.note: rosier, as in a rosier outlook, is more promising

explanation.surface: A tree with better prospects after pruning.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of willow whose pliant shoots are used in basket-making.

clue.text: Reportedly most important feature of lion

indicators.note: reportedly says we hear a word rather than read it

parts.note: main means chief or most important

explanation.surface: A zoo guide stressing the big cat's key characteristic.
explanation.definitionFit: The thick ring of hair round a male lion's head is its best-known feature.

clue.text: Law-breaker's gambit is misplaced

definitions.note: read as 'law-breaker is', the apostrophe s being the link

indicators.note: misplaced says the letters of gambit is are put out of their places

explanation.surface: A chess player's opening move called out as being against the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrying while already wed is a crime, so a person doing it is an offender.

clue.text: Dazzling display in Brazilian port, ahead of time

indicators.note: says the port comes in front of the letter for time

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a major port in Brazil

explanation.surface: Carnival in Rio, a spectacle staged early.
explanation.definitionFit: A riot of colour is a vivid, profuse display, as in a flowerbed.

clue.text: Prepare for performance — again listen by wings of stage

parts.note: re- as a prefix means again
to hear is to listen

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its outermost letters, like a theatre's wings

explanation.surface: An actor listening again from the side of the stage before the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Practising a play or piece before the real show is getting ready for it.
